prompt.en: At a repair fair, a helper with amateur credentials is asked to work on a visitor's transmitter and then test a staff-service channel in the same radio. Which approval note is complete?

text.en: Check the visitor side for the amateur-transmitter work, and treat the staff channel as needing its own service approval instead of borrowing amateur authority.
Approve both tasks once the helper's amateur credential is shown, because the radio can tune both channel groups.
Approve the staff-channel test if the visitor is nearby, even without checking the other service requirements.
Check only the radio's power level, because low power replaces the authorization checks.

explanation.en: Rules combined: B-001-005-003, B-001-005-005, B-001-006-005, B-001-006-006. The helper's credential is only one part of the amateur work check, and non-amateur service use has its own conditions.

prompt.en: A hilltop one-way status signal is proposed, but the same message template would add public sponsor offers during an event. Which revision best applies both station-type and content limits?

text.en: Keep any permitted one-way technical status use separate from messages aimed at the public or serving business content.
Approve all one-way traffic if the signal helps operators judge coverage.
Allow the sponsor offers if the messages use an amateur call sign at the start.
Treat the public-audience and business limits as solved whenever a transmitter is on a hilltop.

explanation.en: Rules combined: B-001-008-002, B-001-007-002, B-001-007-004, B-001-007-011. The one-way station example does not erase the separate limits on public-audience or business messages.

prompt.en: During a school demonstration, the owner signs a permission card, the qualified operator steps away from the controls, and an unlicensed student is ready to transmit. What must happen before the microphone is used?

text.en: Pause until a qualified person is back supervising from the control position; the owner's card does not remove shared responsibility or presence requirements.
Let the student transmit because written permission transfers all station responsibility to the guest.
Let the student transmit if the qualified operator remains somewhere nearby but away from the controls.
Let the student transmit if the station owner promises to review the log afterward.

explanation.en: Rules combined: B-001-009-001, B-001-009-005, B-001-009-006, B-001-009-008, B-001-009-009. Permission, ownership, and later logging do not replace control-point supervision and qualified presence while transmitting.
